nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Your team needs a single managed Azure workspace that lets data scientists train and deploy models with notebooks and the Python SDK, while business analysts use a no-code drag-and-drop designer. Which service fits best?
flashcards.back: Azure Machine Learning is the end-to-end managed ML platform on Azure. It provides Automated ML, the visual Designer, hosted notebooks, the Python/CLI v2 SDK, MLOps pipelines, managed endpoints and a model registry. Databricks is a Spark analytics platform, Synapse is a unified analytics/data-warehouse service, and AI Search powers retrieval scenarios.

flashcards.front: A developer wants to add vision, language, speech and decision features to an app by calling pre-built REST endpoints without training any model. Which family of Azure services should they use?
flashcards.back: Azure AI services (formerly known as Cognitive Services) are pre-built, consumable AI APIs grouped into Vision, Language, Speech and Decision categories. Data Factory is for data movement, Logic Apps for workflow integration, and HDInsight for managed big-data clusters.

flashcards.front: Which type of machine learning is used to predict a continuous numeric value, such as the future selling price of a house from its features?
flashcards.back: Regression is a supervised learning technique that predicts a continuous numeric value (price, temperature, demand). Classification predicts a discrete category, clustering groups unlabeled data, and reinforcement learning learns through rewards from an environment.

flashcards.front: An online retailer wants to automatically segment shoppers by purchase behaviour when no category labels are available. Which machine-learning approach is appropriate?
flashcards.back: Clustering is an unsupervised technique that groups items by feature similarity when no labels are provided; k-means and DBSCAN are common implementations. Classification and regression need labeled training data, and anomaly detection looks for rare outliers rather than producing groupings.

nodes.title: Part 2: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 2. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which feature inside Azure AI Language scores the overall opinion in a passage of text as positive, neutral or negative with a confidence value?
flashcards.back: Sentiment analysis classifies a piece of text as positive, neutral or negative and returns a confidence score; the same feature also supports per-aspect (opinion mining) scoring. Key phrase extraction surfaces the main concepts, NER finds entities such as people, places and dates, and language detection identifies the language.

flashcards.front: A call-centre app must transcribe live customer audio into text in real time. Which Azure AI Speech capability provides this?
flashcards.back: Speech to text converts spoken audio into written text in real time or from recorded files. Text to speech is the inverse (synthesising audio), Speech translation translates spoken input across languages, and Speaker recognition identifies or verifies a person by their voice.

flashcards.front: Your team wants to build a chatbot that answers user questions from an existing collection of FAQs, product documents and support URLs. Which Azure capability is designed for that?
flashcards.back: The question answering feature of Azure AI Language (the successor to QnA Maker) builds a knowledge base from documents, URLs and FAQs and serves natural-language answers, often combined with Azure AI Bot Service. Personalizer ranks content, Metrics Advisor monitors KPI streams, and Anomaly Detector flags time-series outliers.

flashcards.front: A factory wants to flag unusual spikes in equipment-sensor time-series streams without having to train a model. Which Azure AI service is the right fit?
flashcards.back: Azure AI Anomaly Detector is a pre-built decision service that finds anomalies in univariate or multivariate time-series data with little or no ML expertise. The other services handle harmful-content filtering, custom image classification and machine translation.

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An enterprise wants to use OpenAI GPT models inside Azure with regional hosting, private networking, content filters and Microsoft enterprise agreements. Which service should they choose?
flashcards.back: Azure OpenAI Service provides access to OpenAI's GPT, embeddings, DALL-E and Whisper models hosted on Azure with enterprise-grade security, regional availability, content filtering and integration with Azure networking and identity. AI Language covers NLP features, AI Search is a retrieval service, and Bot Service is a conversational framework.

flashcards.front: Which pattern grounds a generative AI model in current private knowledge by fetching relevant passages at inference time and passing them into the prompt, instead of changing the model weights?
flashcards.back: RAG retrieves the most relevant passages (often via vector search in Azure AI Search) and injects them into the prompt so the model answers using current, private content. Fine-tuning changes the weights themselves, RLHF aligns model behaviour through human preference data, and prompt compression simply reduces token usage.

flashcards.front: Which Azure AI service offers content filters that flag hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content in text and images, and is integrated with Azure OpenAI?
flashcards.back: Azure AI Content Safety analyses text and images for harmful categories (hate, violence, self-harm, sexual) with severity levels and supports Prompt Shield and protected-material detection for generative AI scenarios. Personalizer ranks content, Purview governs data, and Translator does machine translation.

flashcards.front: Which Azure service is the natural choice to implement knowledge mining: indexing a large set of documents and enriching them with AI skills (OCR, key phrases, entities) so users can search them?
flashcards.back: Azure AI Search (formerly Cognitive Search) is the knowledge-mining service: it ingests documents from data sources, applies AI skills (OCR, key phrases, entities, vectors) and exposes a queryable index. It is also the typical retriever in RAG patterns. Data Lake stores files, Cosmos DB is a NoSQL database, and Document Intelligence extracts fields from individual forms.
